title: MAPLE-Guard: Memory-Aware Link Enforcement Against Memory-Link Poisoning in Multi-Agent Systems

object.carrier: Persistent agent memory items m=(x,μ) — text records with metadata (content x, access scope, provenance, lifecycle state, guard-side signals) — held in per-agent private stores and shared stores of a memory-augmented multi-agent system; a memory link is the dependency created by write/retrieve/promote/reuse/update operations on such items

safety_property.statement: A poisoned memory item written once must not steer benign agents' later decisions, be promoted into shared memory, or be reused by agents that never saw the original attack; the property fails when an attack-specified target answer/tool is reached (ASR@3) instead of a correct non-target consensus (MDSR@3), and the defense is judged to potentially fail under forged provenance metadata or payloads that stay below per-event risk thresholds.
safety_property.operationalized_as: ASR@3 (fraction of trigger tasks whose final-round aggregated answer equals the attacker target y*) and MDSR@3 (fraction reaching correct, non-target consensus among non-attacker agents) at the final round, scored by an LLM judge (Qwen3.5-122B-A10B, temperature 0), plus propagation diagnostics PMUR / PMUR-A / Sec. ASR@3 (Appendix D)

capabilities: controls one or a few benign-looking agents inside the MAS
writes experience-like poisoned memories through ordinary task interaction (dialogue route)
seeds items directly into a memory store it can reach (direct-memory route)
goal: make a poisoned item survive long enough to steer a benign agent's later decision (targeted attack toward a specific wrong answer or risky tool)
assumptions: attacker cannot modify other agents' private stores
attacker cannot modify the guard's hidden signals φ(m)
attacker cannot modify the communication topology
runtime provenance metadata and retrieval traces are trustworthy
unless stated otherwise, the attacker is unaware of the guard
not_covered: an attacker who can forge source-route, writer, scope, or lineage records (metadata forgery)
payloads designed to remain below per-event risk thresholds
prevention of every initial compromise (guard contains rather than prevents)
generalization to unseen adaptive attacks (one fixed signal/weight/threshold configuration evaluated)
causal isolation of the attack entry point (each benchmark paired with a single attack)

intervention.name: MAPLE-Guard (Memory-Aware Propagation and Link Enforcement Guard)
intervention.description: A lifecycle guard that intercepts every memory-link event and places gates at four checkpoints — a write firewall at storage (reject/quarantine/rewrite/private), a retrieval gate before reasoning (value-aware ranking plus rule-based filter), a promotion gate before an item enters shared memory, and a cross-agent gate before another agent reuses it — each deciding allow/demote/block. Decisions come from one fixed variant-agnostic risk model over eight signals (provenance, lineage, self-claimed success, instruction-likeness, answer binding, trigger sensitivity, cluster dominance, source-agent trust; largest weights on provenance and lineage) computed from the memory text, hidden guard state φ(m) and provenance chain P(m), combined with outcome-conditioned utility/trust updates (Q-value style) after each task; signals are never exposed to the backbone LLM.

results.claim: In the LongMemEval-MemoryGraft setting with Qwen3.5-122B-A10B, MAPLE-Guard raises MDSR@3 from 54.0% to 74.3% and reduces RDA@3 [v2 对 v1 的 ASR@3 改名] from 38.2% to 0.9% (Table 2). v2 补充基线语境：其 RDA 仅比最佳基线 Challenger（2.2%）低 1.3 个百分点，而 PIGuard 的 MDSR 更高（79.1%）但 RDA 5.9%——MAPLE 降低检索损伤但不领先任务成功。
results.setting: LongMemEval-MemoryGraft; 8-agent MAS (3 attacker-controlled), 3 rounds, star/chain/tree topologies, 15 runs per topology, judge Qwen3.5-122B-A10B temperature 0, controlled-topology main grid
results.quote: With Qwen3.5-122B-A10B, MAPLE raises MDSR@3 from 54.0% to 74.3% and reduces RDA@3 from 38.2% to 0.9% (Table 2). Its RDA is 1.3 points below the best baseline (Challenger: 2.2%). PIGuard instead has the highest MDSR (79.1%), with 5.9% RDA: MAPLE lowers retrieval damage but does not lead task success.

denominator.n_total: 200 benchmark instances per run; 15 runs per topology, reported as mean over star/chain/tree topology means
denominator.how_counted: ASR@3 and MDSR@3 are fractions of trigger tasks (attack-successful iff final answer equals attacker target; defense-successful iff correct non-target consensus), Appendix D.1

results.claim: In AppWorld-AgentPoison with Qwen3.5-122B-A10B, MAPLE-Guard raises MDSR@3 from 42.5% to 99.8% and cuts RDA@3 from 34.7% to 0.2%; with gemma-4-31B it reaches 95.3% MDSR@3 and 0.0% RDA@3 [v2 补充 gemma 数值]。
results.setting: AppWorld-AgentPoison; 8-agent MAS (3 attacker-controlled), 3 rounds, star/chain/tree topologies, 15 runs per topology, Qwen3.5-122B-A10B main grid (gemma-4-31B: 95.3% MDSR@3 / 0.0% ASR@3 per §5.5)
results.quote: On AppWorld-AgentPoison, MAPLE-Guard achieves 99.8% MDSR@3 and 0.2% RDA@3 with Qwen3.5-122B-A10B, and 95.3% MDSR@3 and 0.0% RDA@3 with gemma-4-31B.

denominator.n_total: 200 benchmark instances per run; 15 runs per topology, reported as mean over star/chain/tree topology means
denominator.how_counted: ASR@3 and MDSR@3 are fractions of trigger tasks (Appendix D.1)

results.claim: Without any defense, memory-link poisoning is potent: RDA@3 reaches 51.4% on MMLU-MINJA and 34.7% on AppWorld with Qwen3.5-122B-A10B, and 75.1% on MMLU and 84.4% on InjectAgent with gemma-4-31B [v2 将 ASR@3 更名 RDA@3，数值不变]；v2 Obs1 标题强调 gemma 两设置 RDA@3 超过 75%。
results.value: RDA@3 75.1% and 84.4% (gemma); 51.4% and 34.7% (Qwen) [v1 记为 ASR@3]
results.setting: No Defense condition of the main grid; five benchmark-attack settings, 8 agents (3 attacker-controlled), 3 rounds, controlled topologies, both backbones
results.quote: Under No Defense, RDA@3 is 51.4% on MMLU-MINJA and 34.7% on AppWorld with Qwen3.5-122B-A10B, and 75.1% on MMLU and 84.4% on InjectAgent with gemma-4-31B.

denominator.how_counted: ASR@3 is the fraction of trigger tasks whose final-round answer equals the attacker target (Appendix D.1)

results.claim: On AppWorld-AgentPoison with Qwen3.5-122B-A10B, the message-level baseline GUARDIAN backfires and increases RDA from 34.7% (No Defense) to 56.5%, consistent with incomplete coverage of stored-memory paths [v2 措辞]；同时 v2 补充：MMLU 上全部六个 message/topology 级守卫都降低了 RDA。
results.setting: AppWorld-AgentPoison, Qwen3.5-122B-A10B, GUARDIAN baseline vs No Defense, main grid
results.quote: On MMLU with Qwen3.5-122B-A10B, all six message- and topology-level guards reduce RDA relative to No Defense; on AppWorld, however, GUARDIAN increases RDA from 34.7% to 56.5%.

denominator.how_counted: ASR@3 is the fraction of trigger tasks whose final-round answer equals the attacker target (Appendix D.1)

results.claim: In the InjectAgent-ToolAttack transfer setting with Qwen3.5-122B-A10B, the same fixed guard configuration reduces RDA@3 from 20.6%±7.2 (No Defense) to 4.9%±2.7 (Table 2 MAPLE 行；v2 将 ASR@3 更名 RDA@3 且 v1 的 prose 句改由 Obs3 的固定配置论述承担)：信号函数、权重与阈值跨五个攻击设置保持固定，无攻击特定参数搜索。
results.setting: InjectAgent-ToolAttack transfer setting, Qwen3.5-122B-A10B (gemma-4-31B: 56.1% ASR@3 per Table 1), fixed guard configuration without attack-specific tuning
results.quote: On Qwen3.5-122B-A10B, MAPLE-Guard achieves the lowest mean RDA@3 in four settings, including 0.3%, 0.9%, and 0.2% on MMLU, LongMemEval, and AppWorld, respectively. The signal functions, weights, and thresholds remain fixed without attack-specific parameter search.

results.claim: In the single-gate ablation on LongMemEval-MemoryGraft (outcome feedback retained in every variant), removing the promotion gate causes the largest degradation, reducing MDSR@3 from 73.6% to 60.0% and raising RDA@3 from 0.9% to 14.5% [v1 记 73.60/60.00/14.50，v2 改为一位小数]；去掉 write/retrieval/cross-agent 门产生较小但一致的损失。v2 新增 matched-lifecycle 对照：full guard 88.4%/0.1% vs retrieval-only 65.0%/21.6%（AppWorld 代理，Gemma Base）。
results.setting: LongMemEval-MemoryGraft; one lifecycle gate removed at a time while retaining the outcome-conditioned update; remaining write/retrieval/cross-agent ablations give smaller consistent losses
results.quote: The full guard achieves 73.6% MDSR@3 and 0.9% RDA@3. Removing the promotion gate causes the largest degradation, reducing MDSR@3 to 60.0% and increasing RDA@3 to 14.5%; removing the write, retrieval, or cross-agent gate produces smaller but consistent losses.

denominator.n_total: 200 benchmark instances per run; 15 runs per topology, reported as mean over star/chain/tree topology means
denominator.how_counted: ASR@3 and MDSR@3 are fractions of trigger tasks (Appendix D.1; a benign mistake counts toward neither, so they are not complementary). The ablation keeps the main-grid evaluation protocol: the full-guard reference (73.60%/0.90%) equals the Table 1 / Appendix C LongMemEval-MemoryGraft main-grid cell (200 benchmark instances per run, eight agents of which three are attacker-controlled, 15 runs per topology, averaged over star/chain/tree topology means), and Appendix D.2 states the ablation removes one lifecycle gate at a time under the same outcome update. No separate ablation instance count is printed; soft corroboration: 60.00% and 14.50% of 200 are integer counts (120/29).

results.claim: Benign utility: under random topology, MAPLE changes MDSR by −1.5 (MMLU), +7.0 (LongMemEval), +1.0 (AppWorld), +1.4 (CSQA), +0.9 (InjectAgent) points on Qwen — Table 6 行值与 v1 一致（MMLU 88.5→87.0，AppWorld 99.0→100.0）。v2 明确改口：the guard is not uniformly cost-free（两骨干在 MMLU 均失 1.5 点，gemma 在 LongMemEval 失 1.4 点）；v2 新增 token 审计：MAPLE 在 MMLU/InjectAgent 上相对 No Defense 减少 35.0%/27.8% 的测量 token 用量，且无额外 guard-LLM 调用。
results.value: MMLU 87.0 vs 88.5; AppWorld 100.0 vs 99.0; MMLU −1.5 pt on both backbones
results.setting: Attack-free benign utility under random topology, Qwen3.5-122B-A10B backbone (gemma-4 columns: MMLU 56.5 -> 55.0, LongMemEval 34.2 -> 32.8)
results.quote: Thus the guard is not uniformly cost-free: both backbones lose 1.5 points on MMLU, and gemma also loses 1.4 points on LongMemEval.

denominator.how_counted: Attack-free MDSR@3 (%) under random topology per benchmark, No Defense -> MAPLE (Table 6); five benchmarks x two backbones; token audit on five fixed tasks per benchmark, eight agents, three rounds, one fixed random adjacency and seed, 128-token generation limit

limitations.statement: MAPLE-Guard contains memory-link poisoning after it enters the system rather than preventing every initial compromise.
limitations.quote: MAPLE-Guard is designed to contain memory-link poisoning after it enters the system rather than prevent every initial compromise.

limitations.statement: The guard assumes reliable provenance metadata and retrieval traces; forged metadata or below-threshold payloads may evade it.
limitations.quote: It assumes reliable provenance metadata and retrieval traces; forged metadata or payloads designed to remain below per-event thresholds may evade the guard.

limitations.statement: Because each benchmark is paired with a single attack, the evaluation cannot isolate the causal effect of the attack entry point.
limitations.quote: because each benchmark is paired with a single attack, the evaluation supports within-benchmark comparisons among defenses but does not isolate the causal effect of the attack entry point.

limitations.statement: v2 Limitation 重写：固定单一信号/权重/阈值配置的跨设置表现仍成立（Obs3），但新增两条 caveat——完整反馈设定使用 benchmark-evaluator 结果作为反馈源；CSQA transfer runner 的部分运行时元数据由已知攻击者角色初始化；且每个 benchmark 只配一种攻击，评估支持基准内对比而不能分离攻击入口的因果效应
limitations.quote: Finally, because each benchmark is paired with a single attack, the evaluation supports within-benchmark comparisons among defenses but does not isolate the causal effect of the attack entry point.
